prediction.likelyOutcome: Dover Mall should win on liability as a matter of law -- Tang's COVID frustration/impossibility and pre-pandemic occupancy-decline defenses both fail against the lease's explicit force-majeure carve-out for rent and the independent nature of the rent covenant. The real uncertainty is whether the court awards the full $276,089.72 on summary judgment or finds the landlord's unsubstantiated mitigation record creates a triable issue on amount; either way, a substantial majority of the requested sum is the likely outcome, capped at the $276,089.72 actually prayed for.

outcome.description: The Superior Court granted the landlord summary judgment on liability and damages in the amount of $276,089.72, the full amount demanded, holding the force majeure clause allocated pandemic-closure risk to the tenant and two lease provisions relieved the landlord of any duty to relet. No attorney's fee award is stated. This is a trial-level decision; no appeal is reflected in the opinion.
